text.p: Ekran Bhd said on Wednesday that its rights offering drew a subscription rate that was 62.77 percent below the total number of 257,143,286 shares available for subscription.

In a statement, the main promoter of the $6.2 billion Bakun hydro-electric dam also said its executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing has agreed to buy 150,984,271 rights issue shares from several of the underwriters, boosting his stake in the company to 55.7 percent from 26.3 percent.
Ting's purchase of the one-for-one rights was at 5.70 ringgit per share.

The rights issue had been expected to be undersubscribed because of a weak Malaysian stock market and concerns over the Bakun project, which is being built in the jungles of Sarawak state on Borneo island.
It said that at the close of acceptance and payment of the rights issue on May 26, total acceptance and excess shares applications amounting to 95,725,542 shares were received.
The unsubscribed shares have been fully underwritten by a consortium of underwriters, the statement said.
In connection with Ting's purchase of the rights, he has sought a waiver from having to make a general offer for Ekran shares not already owned by him and his wife.
Ekran said the Securities Commission and the Foreign Investment Committee have respectively granted the waiver subject to certain conditions.
The conditions include Ting and his wife having to reduce their Ekran stake to less than 33 percent within 24 months from the date of the rights issue share acquisitions.
The Securities Commission also requires Ting to cut his stake through placing the shares to buyers approved by the Ministry of Finance.
Ting and "parties acting in concert with him" have also agreed not to increase their shareholdings in Ekran until the reduction in the stake to under 33 percent within two years has been fulfilled.
Ekran said Ting has accepted the conditions of the Securities Commission's waiver.
Ekran's stock has been suspended for the company announcement. It closed down 15 cents to 5.50 ringgit on Monday.
